author: Admin101
title: Southern California Event: Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire
content:
The Los Angeles Local of Black Rose/Rosa Negra announces this public event on anarchist histories of the past and present in Southern California’s Inland Empire.




Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire 

will explore contemporary anarchism, especifismo, popular power, and local labor struggles and social movements in the Inland Empire.




This panel discussion features local historians Troy Andreas Araiza Kokinis, author of 

Anarchist Popular Power

, and Kevan Antonio Aguilar.




When:

 Friday November 13th • 6:30 PM




Where:

 Pain Sugar Gallery • 3635 9th St, Riverside, CA 92501




Cost:

 No cost, donations for literature accepted.













The post 

Southern California Event: Towards an Anarchist History in the Inland Empire

 appeared first on 

Black Rose/Rosa Negra Anarchist Federation

.

author: Admin101
title: Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense
content:
Black Rose/Rosa Negra Anarchist Federation (BRRN) is excited to announce the publication of 

Sanctuary as a Verb: Experiences and Directions from Transversal Organizing for Immigrant Defense

.




Drawing on organizing experiences of Black Rose/Rosa Negra members across the United States, this pamphlet explores how workers, neighbors, and communities are building collective resistance to ICE and defending their immigrant coworkers, classmates, and loved ones. By connecting struggles across workplaces, schools, and neighborhoods, the 

transversal organizing

 approach we prioritize builds solidarity across different sectors of society to confront the interconnected structures of domination that shape our lives.




You can find a downloadable PDF version of the pamphlet at the end of this text.







Two Years of Trump II: Immigrants in the Crosshairs, Resistance Under Attack
